newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica buying group seeks 250,000 T maize imports.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica buying group seeks 250,000 T maize imports.

text.p: South Africa's Western Cape Buyers Association said on Monday it planned to import 250,000 tonnes of yellow maize this season and next.

Due to a shortage of yellow maize this season, caused by excessive exports, the group said it had decided to invite tenders for the delivery of 30,000 tonnes of maize in February, 40,000 in March and 60,000 in April. The April consignment has already been contracted.

The group also said it had decided to tender for Argentine maize for delivery in the new season, starting May 1, 1997, in view of calls by the National Maize Producers' Organisation that farmers scale down their plantings.
The association said it would seek delivery of 40,000 tonnes during May, 40,000 tonnes during June and 40,000 during July.
A decision on the allocation of tenders will be made within the next fortnight.

The group said the department of agriculture had recently issued a permit for the import of maize from the U.S. and the first shipment of 35,000 tonnes was expected early in January "at a landed cost significantly lower than that offered by the local market".
